items.q: There were a few big ones like Martin Block and Al Jarvis out on the coast

ctx.x: At that point were records licensed for radio broadcast? They weren't were they? You had to --

Well, this is the thing that Fred Waring fought for years and got nowhere. But the fact remains that a record is a form of publication. For example, you can get in ASCAP if you've got a record of a tune, whether you have anything printed or not. You say here's the record. They recognize that as a form of publication. And therefore, if you own the -- if you bought the record you can do anything you want with it. Now, Fred was trying to say that everybody should get paid when they played the record on the radio.…
